title: KV: page rejuvenation and eviction fairness controller
author: Marisol Ortega
release_notes: Improves KV cache memory reclamation and eviction fairness; reduced tail latency in mixed-tenancy workloads. No public API changes.
description:
Motivation: Heavy continuous-batching workloads in production exposed two correlated issues in our KV cache: (1) fragmentation and short-lived page churn that causes premature paging/IO spikes, and (2) eviction imbalances across tenants and request classes where aggressive clients consumed disproportionate residency, causing noisy neighbor P95/P99 regressions.

Summary: Introduce a lightweight "Page Rejuvenation" pass plus an Eviction Fairness Controller (EFC) that cooperates with the runtime scheduler and pager to (a) bias evictions away from recently-rejuvenated pages, (b) smooth pager activity to avoid IO bursts during large compactions/spill, and (c) enforce proportional eviction quotas so tenants with similar footprint receive fair residency reclamation over time. The feature integrates kernel-selection hints for compact vs. fast-evict paths and exposes observability for eviction debt and rejuvenation throughput.

Implementation details: The change set includes: 1) pkg/kv/reclaimer.go — implements page-ageing, a rejuvenation worker that performs low-cost liveness sampling and optionally issues compact hints to the allocator; 2) pkg/kv/eviction_controller.go — the EFC that tracks per-tenant eviction debt, computes fair quotas, and generates prioritized eviction plans; 3) pkg/kv/pager_smoother.go — a rate limiter/backpressure layer for the pager to turn bursts into steady drain, with hooks for the scheduler to temporarily reduce batching pressure; 4) pkg/runtime/kernel_selector.go — adds a new compact-vs-evict heuristic to pick optimized kernel paths depending on sequence length and page locality; 5) instrumentation and dashboards (metrics exported: kv_rejuvenation_ops_total, evict_quota_utilization, pager_smooth_latency_histogram).

Backwards compatibility and rollout: All behaviors are behind two feature flags: kv.page_rejuvenation and kv.eviction_fairness. Defaults: page_rejuvenation=on; eviction_fairness=gradual (soft enforcement). We plan a canary rollout in us-west-2 for 48 hours followed by a fleet-wide ramp. No changes to client-facing APIs.

Testing and benchmarks: Unit tests for the controller logic and fuzzer cases for eviction invariants were added. Bench harness: internal/bench/kv_reclaim_bench.go — shows median token-per-second improvement ~3.8% on mixed read/write traces with P99 latency reduced by ~12% in noisy-neighbor scenarios. Bench results attached in CI artifacts.

Related work: follows on prior allocator work (ENG-1623) and complements the spill-smoothing series; related Linear tickets: ENG-2345 (eviction fairness design), ENG-2411 (pager stability).

Checklist: referenced design doc, added metrics, added unit + integration tests, feature flags present, documented rollout and rollback steps in docs/design/kv-eviction-fairness.md.

merge_commit_message:
feat(kv): page rejuvenation + eviction fairness controller (ENG-2345)

- rejuvenation worker for low-cost liveness hints
- eviction fairness quotas to reduce noisy neighbor regressions
- pager smoothing to avoid IO spikes

See docs/design/kv-eviction-fairness.md for details
summary_of_changes: Adds a rejuvenation pass to reduce fragmentation, an Eviction Fairness Controller to balance evictions across tenants, pager smoothing to reduce IO bursts, and kernel hints to optimize compaction vs eviction paths. Includes tests, benches, and docs.
